title: sdk docs scratchpad - onboarding tutorial fixes
content:
Quick scratchpad for quick wins on the SDK docs + onboarding tutorial.

Top-level goals:
- Fix clarity gaps in 'Getting started' (esp. auth flow + region selection)
- Add a minimal sample app (node + python) that shows streaming + function-calling
- Shorten the tutorial: split beginner vs intermediate paths
- Add CI check that samples run in headless mode (no visual/manual steps)

TODO (prioritized):
1) Auth + region quicknote (high)
   - Problem: current guide buries region selection behind footnote; users pick default region and get 403s.
   - Action: add a 2-line section at top showing ENV vars: REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_REGION.
   - Acceptance: follow steps on fresh account -> success with curl + node example.

2) Minimal node sample app (high)
   - Create /examples/node-streaming-app: single-file index.js that streams completions from hosted API and prints latency per chunk.
   - Keep deps minimal (node 18+, axios or fetch).
   - Include README with run steps and expected output snippet.
   - Linked PR: github PR/492 notes sample scaffold.

3) Python sample (medium)
   - Simple Flask app that calls streaming chat and demonstrates function-calling.
   - Note: show how to run with Uvicorn for local dev.

4) Tutorial flow cleanup (medium)
   - Split into "Start here" (10 min) and "Build an app" (30-60 min).
   - Move advanced options (batching, quantization notes) to an "ops" appendix.

5) Add tests for samples (low)
   - Headless smoke test script that runs examples with a mock API key and asserts exit code 0.

Open questions / blockers:
- Need confirmation on default region name for hosted orgs (us-west-2 vs us-central-1). Pinged infra on slack #platform-infra.
- Do we want to show Dedicated/Private code paths in the same tutorial or link to separate pages? My preference: separate primer pages and a note pointing to them.

Notes to self (copy into PR description):
- Keep examples under /examples in repo; avoid duplicating content in docs (link instead).
- Use plain fetch/requests examples first, then SDK wrappers as optional.
- Add metrics snippet for Console tracing (how to enable client-side tracing header X-Redwood-Trace).

Small code snippet to include in node sample (for authoring):
// index.js (streaming example)
// pseudo-code, final will use fetch with ReadableStream
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, region: process.env.REDWOOD_REGION });
const stream = await client.stream.chat({ model: 'redwood/gpt-4-mini', messages: [{role:'user', content:'Hello'}] });
for await (const chunk of stream) {
  process.stdout.write(chunk.text);
}

Estimated time: 2-3 days for the quick wins (items 1+2), additional 3-4 days for python sample, tests, and tutorial split.

Next steps (this week):
- Wed: land quick auth + region note + tiny README (small PR)
- Thu: push node example and smoke test (PR with travis/github action)
- Fri: review with Alex and Sam, decide on Dedicated/Private doc approach

Notes to future me: keep the language simple; avoid internal jargon. If users hit 403 mention region mismatch in the error troubleshooting section.

End of scratchpad.
